title: Chain to a Wave Theory
caption: A chain: the article builds, step by step, from a flaw in the old wiring-diagram model of the brain through oscillation-based mechanisms to a wave theory of cognition, then uses that theory to explain analog computation and finally consciousness itself — each stage resting on the one above it.

scenes.title: From fixed wiring to wave-based mind

items.text: Fixed-wiring model can't explain it
items.sub: a third of neurons fire on any task
items.detail: Classic feedforward, specialist-neuron models cannot explain why so many prefrontal neurons respond to almost every task.

items.text: Neurons multitask (mixed selectivity)
items.sub: same neuron, different meaning by context
items.detail: Many cortical neurons blend sensory, motor and context signals, so a fixed synaptic map can't be the whole story.

items.text: Brain waves organize and route spikes
items.detail: Oscillations segregate and time spiking, and gate which regions can talk to which.

items.text: Waves push spikes directly (ephaptic coupling)
items.detail: Electric fields alter nearby neurons' voltage without using a synapse, fast and over a wide area.

items.text: Alpha/beta waves as inhibitory 'stencils'
items.detail: Spatial patterns of alpha/beta suppress gamma-driven spiking in some places, letting it through elsewhere.

items.text: Explains mixed selectivity and subspace coding
Moving waves shift neural coding states
items.detail: Traveling alpha/beta waves accompany the brain switching from one activity pattern to another.

items.text: Wave interference = analog computation
items.detail: Overlapping waves add, cancel and combine, doing math in parallel without digital steps.

items.text: Far more energy-efficient than digital
Anesthesia disrupts wave organization, not specific cells
items.detail: Very different drugs all converge on the same slow, desynchronized cortical waves when consciousness is lost.

items.text: Synapses store, waves decide what's active now
Vs. Global Workspace, IIT, Higher-Order theories

scenes.caption: Down the page is the article's own order: a problem with the classical model leads to oscillations and ephaptic coupling, which feed a wave-based control theory, which explains moving brain states and analog computing, which together are used to explain consciousness and unconsciousness.

scenes.title: Inside: Spatial Computing Theory

items.text: Alpha/beta as inhibitory stencils
items.detail: Spatially patterned alpha/beta rhythms suppress gamma-driven spiking in some cortical locations while sparing others, routing information without the brain needing to track specific synapses.

items.text: Alpha/beta's millimeter scale fits top-down control
items.detail: Gamma is too fine-grained, theta/delta too broad; alpha/beta sits at the right spatial scale, and in primates it does encode context and predicts errors.

items.text: Produces mixed selectivity
items.detail: A neuron inside the stencil in one context but outside it in another looks like it has switched its tuning, without any fixed context-detecting cells.

items.text: Produces orthogonal subspace coding
items.detail: The stencils split spiking into separate, structured subsets of active neurons, which is what low-dimensional 'subspace' coding looks like.

scenes.caption: A hub: the central idea (alpha/beta waves as stencils that suppress or permit gamma spiking) has three things it is used to explain, shown as satellites rather than a strict sequence.

scenes.title: Inside: Traveling Waves and Analog Computation

items.text: Beta waves travel across motor cortex before/after movement
items.detail: Beta rhythms, which brake movement, rise and fall as a moving wave timed to movement onset and offset.

items.text: Traveling waves may drive switches between coding states
items.detail: Moving patterns of inhibition/excitation could transition population activity from one orthogonal subspace to another.

items.text: Analog computing: continuous physical quantities do the math
items.detail: Instead of binary signals, waves directly add, cancel and combine — the physics itself performs the calculation.

items.text: Whole pattern settles at once, all in parallel
items.sub: far cheaper than step-by-step digital logic
items.detail: Because the medium evolves everywhere simultaneously, analog wave computation is inherently parallel and energy-efficient.

items.text: Example: summing two context-waves gives a unique pattern per combination
items.detail: Two task-context signals, each a wave pattern, sum to produce a distinct neural pattern for every combination of contexts — an 'intersection of constraints.'

scenes.caption: A chain: moving waves are shown to drive state changes, which is then reframed as a form of computation, which is argued to be efficient and used for combining task contexts.
